segments.text: Hi everyone, welcome back to Synthetic Biology One.
Today we will be measuring DNA concentration by absorption.
The principle of this protocol is that DNA absorbs UV light.
Actually different nucleotides absorb wavelengths,
a little bit different wavelengths, but the overall peak is around 260
nanometers. We will be using a tabletop
spectrophotometer commonly named Nanodrop.
So first I will have to run a blank using the same solution as you used
for the dilution of the DNA. In this case it's water.
So I will put 1.5 microliters of water and click blank.
Okay now that the blank is made I can load
the sample, but before that I will wipe
the measuring area with a clean tissue, and now I can load 1.5 microliters
of the sample. Make sure that there's no bubbles.
Okay and so you can see that there's a prominent peak at 260 nanometers
which corresponds to the DNA. And the concentration that is measured at
this peak is around 200 nanograms per microliters.
However it is also important to look at peaks
around 230 and 280 nanometers, because this corresponds to wavelengths
at which possible impurities will absorb. In this case there's no peak
at these wavelengths, meaning that the DNA is pure and
the concentration corresponds to the concentration of the DNA.
However one common mistake is to measure DNA concentration from the
unpurified PCR samples. Let me show you what kind of results
it will give. So I will load 1.5 microliters
of a non-purified PCR sample, click measure. So you can see
that not only there's a peak at 230 nanometers,
but also the peak, the main peak is shifted from 260
towards 280 nanometers. So this corresponds
to impurities such as proteins, salts and other components of the mix.
Another point is that even though the concentration is measured, you cannot
take this concentration as the actual concentration of your
amplified DNA in the mix, because not only
amplified DNA strands will absorb at this wavelength, but also unused
dNTPs, which means that this concentration does not correspond to the
concentration of your PCR product. So our DNA sample was concentrated and
pure and so the measurement was successful.
Until next time, stay concentrated.
